title: Finite-twist supported Kummer inputs and normalized compact realization over any field
statement:
Let $K_0$ be any field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $K_0$, $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_F$ and uniformizer $\varpi_F$, $n\geq1$, and $A=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $B$ be a separated finite-type $K_0$-scheme and $\pi:E\to B$ a rank-one vector bundle with zero section $z$ [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]; Then $\pi$ is separated of finite type; locally the pair is $(\operatorname{Spec}R[t],V(t))$. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], their comparison pullback $\nu_T^*$ [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], and the prescribed pro-etale twist $A_T(1)$ [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. For each $K_0$-scheme $T$, put $N=\ell^n$ and
$$L_T=\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{N,T}\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z/N}A_T.$$
Here $NA=0$, and $L_T$ agrees with the ordinary tensor product and is a finite locally constant locally free rank-one $A_T$-module sheaf. The projection from the inverse limit of roots induces the specified isomorphism $\alpha_T:\nu_T^*L_T\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T(1)$ [lem-amb-tate-root-projection-reduction]. The complex $A_T(1)[2]$ has finite Tor amplitude contained in $[-2,-2]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]; for $T=E$ it is bounded constructible, and hence belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(E,A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility].

The zero divisor $D=z(B)$ is effective Cartier. Let
$$c_D^e:z_*A_B\longrightarrow L_E[2],\qquad c_D^p:z_*A_B\longrightarrow A_E(1)[2]$$
be the ordinary etale and prescribed pro-etale supported Kummer morphisms [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer, lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map]. Under the canonical supported-constant comparison and $\alpha_E[2]$, the actual morphism $\nu_E^*c_D^e$ equals $c_D^p$. Both supported direct images satisfy $Rz_*=z_*$. For every morphism $g:B'\to B$ of $K_0$-schemes, including nonflat and non-Noetherian base changes, $D'=z'(B')$ remains Cartier, the corresponding supported direct images still satisfy $Rz'_*=z'_*$ on both sites, and pullback of $c_D^e,c_D^p$ gives $c_{D'}^e,c_{D'}^p$ under the supported-constant and roots-projection twist comparisons. These comparisons also apply to isomorphisms of the resulting Cartier pairs, in particular a basis identifying a geometric fibre line with the affine line and its origin.

Choose a compactification of $\pi$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] and the associated compact-support functors [def-amb-etale-compact-support, def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Let $a_\pi^{\mathrm{et}}:A_B\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi_!^{\mathrm{et}}z_*A_B$ and $a_\pi^{\mathrm{proet}}:A_B\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi_!^{\mathrm{proet}}z_*A_B$ be the identity-normalized source isomorphisms of [lem-pur-section-compact-source-exchange] for $(h,s)=(\pi,z)$: on the etale site the proper/open and direct-image composite for $\pi z=1_B$, on the pro-etale site canonical composition [thm-sf-comp-composition]. Let $\tau_E^e=R\pi_!^{\mathrm{et}}(c_D^e)\circ a_\pi^{\mathrm{et}}:A_B\to R\pi_!^{\mathrm{et}}L_E[2]$ and $\tau_E^p=R\pi_!^{\mathrm{proet}}(c_D^p)\circ a_\pi^{\mathrm{proet}}:A_B\to R\pi_!^{\mathrm{proet}}A_E(1)[2]$ be the compact images of $c_D^e,c_D^p$. The canonical comparison $T_\pi:R\pi_!^{\mathrm{proet}}A_E(1)[2]\xrightarrow{\sim}\nu_B^*(R\pi_!^{\mathrm{et}}L_E[2])$ of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] identifies their actual morphisms:
$$T_\pi\circ\tau_E^p=\nu_B^*(\tau_E^e),$$
with its source comparison equal to $1_{A_B}$. These assertions hold over every $K_0$, with no algebraic-closedness or finite-type assumption on $K_0$ over a smaller field. In particular they apply anew over any geometric fibre field $\Omega$, to $B=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $E=\mathbf A^1_\Omega$. No compact-support exchange under $g$, nor any identification of supported with compact cohomology, is asserted here.

source.place: Step 2 first paragraph (geometric fibre class) and Step 3 (Cartier and Kummer pullback): coefficient and site realization extracted from lem-pur-line-zero-class-exchange old steps 1--2, 6--7

proof.text: The field $K_0$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and $K_0$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $B$ Noetherian. Apply [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section] in rank one: a frame over $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ identifies $E|_U$ with $\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$, and the augmentation with $t\mapsto0$. In particular $z$ is closed and $\pi z=1_B$. By [lem-amb-vector-projective-completion], $\pi$ is separated of finite type and $E$ is Noetherian. Composition in [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e) also makes $E$ separated of finite type over $K_0$, as needed below.

source.place: Step 1: vector-bundle geometry and compactification hypotheses

proof.text: By [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $A$ is a finite commutative ring. The absolute value on $F$ restricts to the $\ell$-adic one, so $|\ell|_F=\ell^{-1}<1$. The maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_F$ is $\varpi_F\mathcal O_F$ by that same definition; hence $\ell=\varpi_F b$ for some $b\in\mathcal O_F$. Therefore $\ell^n=\varpi_F^n b^n$ vanishes in $A$. Put $N=\ell^n$, which is invertible on every $K_0$-scheme. Apply [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] first with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z/N$ and then with $A$: $\mu_{N,T}^{\mathrm{et}}$ is a flat locally free $\mathbf Z/N$-line and its ordinary tensor with $A_T$ is a locally constant locally free $A_T$-line. The flat degree-zero tensor comparison [lem-pur-flat-single-derived-normalization], with the symmetry of sheaf tensor, identifies its derived tensor with that ordinary tensor. Thus it is precisely $L_T$, including its finite stalks. Flatness is used for the root sheaf, not for $A$ over $\mathbf Z/N$.

source.place: Step 2: arbitrary finite coefficient level, ordinary etale twist

proof.text: Write $\sigma_{N,T}:\nu_T^*L_T\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_{N,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A_T$ for [lem-amb-finite-root-site-comparison]. Let $\theta_{n,T}:A_T(1)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_{N,T}^{\mathrm{pro}}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A_T$ be [lem-amb-tate-root-projection-reduction], whose annihilation hypothesis is Step 2. Set $\alpha_T=\theta_{n,T}^{-1}\sigma_{N,T}$. This specifies its direction and its normalization: $\theta_{n,T}$ sends a root-limit tensor $x\otimes a$ to $p_{n,T}(x)\otimes a$, and $\sigma$ sends an etale root to that same unit. Both cited statements give their pullback equations for every scheme morphism; composing these equations gives the pullback equation for $\alpha$. Etale covers are also pro-etale covers, so Step 2 and this comparison make $A_T(1)$ locally constant and locally free of rank one, with finite stalks.

source.place: Step 2: specified roots-projection realization and arbitrary scheme pullback

proof.text: A locally free rank-one sheaf is flat: on a trivializing cover its tensor functor is the identity, and exactness of sheaves is local. Apply [lem-pur-flat-single-derived-normalization] on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $L=A_T(1)$. For every module sheaf $M$ in degree zero, $A_T(1)[2]\otimes_A^L M$ is the ordinary tensor sheaf placed in degree $-2$. Thus it has no cohomology outside $[-2,-2]$, exactly the definition in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. On $E$, the sole possible cohomology sheaf is locally constant with finite stalks by Step 3. The one-stratum partition $E=E$ therefore meets [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], and the shift is bounded. Hence $A_E(1)[2]\in D^b_{ctf}(E,A)$. This uses the stated constructibility condition, without introducing a finite-field restriction on $K_0$.

source.place: Step 2: bounded constructibility and Tor window required for later compact-fibre callers

proof.text: In every chart of Step 1 the ideal of $D$ is $(t)$. Multiplication by $t$ on $R[t]$ is injective by comparison of coefficients, and $R[t]/(t)=R$. Thus $D$ is effective Cartier. After any $g:B'\to B$, cover the inverse images of these base opens by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}R'$. The resulting pair is $(\operatorname{Spec}R'[t],V(t))$: the old coordinate changes $t_i=u_{ij}t_j$ pull back to the same equations with units $g^*u_{ij}$. The coefficient argument still makes $t$ a nonzerodivisor, even when $R'$ is nonreduced or non-Noetherian. The complementary open immersion is quasi-compact: locally on its target it is the principal open $D(t)\subset\operatorname{Spec}R'[t]$. This property concerns the immersion, not quasi-compactness of the entire scheme $B'$. The same statements hold before pullback.

source.place: Step 3: Cartier-preserving arbitrary base change of the zero section

proof.text: On either original or pulled-back pair, etale closed pushforward is exact by [lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction]. Its assertion for abelian sheaves gives the module assertion too, since kernels, cokernels and exactness of module sheaves are detected on the underlying abelian sheaves. Pro-etale closed pushforward over the finite constant ring $A$ is exact by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact], since Step 5 verified the quasi-compact complement even after arbitrary $g$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] to these exact functors: on the degree-zero supported coefficients their canonical right-derived functors equal the underived direct images. This proves $Rz_*=z_*$ and $Rz'_*=z'_*$ on both sites.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: exactness of supported direct images for the original and arbitrary pulled-back pairs

proof.text: Apply [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] with $N=\ell^n$ and the Cartier pair from Step 5; Step 2 checks finiteness and $NA=0$. Step 6 identifies its source $Rz_*A_B$ with $z_*A_B$, and Step 2 identifies its target with $L_E[2]$, giving $c_D^e$. The last sentence of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] identifies the same supported etale morphism on this witness with the prescribed pro-etale $c_D^p$. Its target identification is exactly $\alpha_E[2]$ of Step 3. Its source comparison is the canonical supported-constant one; [lem-pur-supported-constant-exchange-normalization] specifies that comparison by preservation of constant restriction. Consequently the equality is of the actual arrows. Both Kummer statements give pullback for every morphism whose pulled-back divisor remains Cartier; Step 5 verifies this for every $g$ in the item. Combine these equations with the root comparison equations in Step 3 and the supported-constant comparison square in the normalization lemma. This gives the asserted pullback identities on both sites, with no finiteness or flatness assumption on $g$. An isomorphism of Cartier pairs is also such a morphism, so the same argument applies to a chosen fibre basis.

source.place: Steps 2 and 3: actual supported Kummer arrows, site comparison, and Cartier pullback

proof.text: Use the chosen compactification and apply [lem-pur-section-compact-source-exchange] with $h=\pi$ and $s=z$. Step 1 verifies its separated finite-type field-scheme hypotheses and its closed-section hypothesis. It supplies the specified $a_\pi^{\mathrm{et}},a_\pi^{\mathrm{proet}}$ and says that the canonical compact-site comparison $T_M$ at $M=z_*A_B$ satisfies $T_M a_\pi^{\mathrm{proet}}=\nu_B^*a_\pi^{\mathrm{et}}$, with identity coefficient source. On the etale site this uses its proper/open and direct-image composite; on the pro-etale site it uses the composition for $\pi z=1_B$. Thus no unidentified automorphism of $A_B$ enters either definition of $\tau$.

source.place: Step 1 and Step 3: identity-normalized compact image of the supported section

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] with $f=\pi$ and the bounded-below etale witness $L_E[2]$ of Step 3. Apply its naturality to the witnessed morphism $c_D^e$ of Step 7, whose source witness is $z_*A_B$ in degree zero. Writing $T_K=T_\pi$, its naturality equation is
$$T_K\,R\pi_!^{\mathrm{proet}}(c_D^p)=
u_B^*(R\pi_!^{\mathrm{et}}c_D^e)\,T_M.$$
Compose on the right with $a_\pi^{\mathrm{proet}}$ and substitute Step 8. The result is $T_\pi	au_E^p=
u_B^*(R\pi_!^{\mathrm{et}}c_D^e)
u_B^*a_\pi^{\mathrm{et}}=
u_B^*	au_E^e$. Finally, every field-dependent input above assumes only that $K_0$ is a field with $\ell$ invertible. Reapply the argument with $K_0=\Omega$, $B=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and the trivial line to obtain the geometric-field assertion; it does not require $\Omega$ finite type over the old field. This step compares the compact images on the two sites, and makes no identification with supported cohomology.
